title: Refraction
target: Connect a change in wave speed to wavelength and direction.
criteria: Measure ray angles from the normal.
Explain frequency continuity at a stationary boundary.
Predict bending toward or away from the normal.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A ray makes 25° with a flat boundary surface. What is its angle from the normal?
cpa.guide: The normal is perpendicular to the surface: 90 − 25 = 65°.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A student measures a ray angle from the surface while the refraction rule uses the normal. What should be corrected?
options: Use the perpendicular-to-surface reference before comparing angles.
Use any reference because angles never depend on it.
cpa.guide: Refraction angles are conventionally measured from the normal.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A 7 Hz wave crosses a stationary boundary into a slower medium. What is its frequency there?
options: Less than 7 Hz solely because speed falls.
Greater than 7 Hz solely because speed falls.
cpa.guide: The driving oscillation rate stays continuous across a stationary boundary.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A wave has frequency 4 Hz and speed changes from 20 to 12 m/s at a stationary boundary. What are wavelengths before and after?
cpa.guide: λ = v/f; frequency stays 4 Hz, so wavelengths are 20/4 and 12/4.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A ray enters a slower medium obliquely, with ordinary positive refractive indices. Which way does it bend?
cpa.guide: Lower wave speed produces a smaller angle to the normal in ordinary refraction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A ray enters a faster medium at an angle below any critical-angle condition. Which change is expected?
options: It bends toward the normal and frequency doubles.
It bends away from the normal while frequency stays the same.
Its speed cannot change between media.
cpa.guide: Faster transmitted speed gives a larger normal angle; the stationary boundary preserves frequency.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
